The following trends have contributed to the results of our operations, and we anticipate that they will continue to affect our future results:

There is a clear growing preference for delivery and take-out, and we expect this trend to continue positively, influencing our operating results, as more customers will need packaging and containers to support the rising demand from food delivery and take-out consumers.

We believe this trend will have a positive long-lasting impact on our results of operations, as we expect there will be an increased demand for eco-friendly and compostable single-use disposable products.
Elevated ocean freight rates could pressure our gross margin, and if we raise our prices, dampen the demand for our products.

We believe this trend will have either a positive or a negative impact on our results of operations, depending on whether we are able to continue to strengthen our global supply chain, whether any previously imposed tariffs are removed and whether we can implement procedures to mitigate the impact from the tariffs.

We believe price fluctuations and the availability of raw materials will have either a positive or a negative impact on our results of operations in the future, depending on whether raw material costs increase or decrease, whether we can successfully implement price adjustments to maintain gross margin and whether we can effectively realign our global supply chain to mitigate disruptions and support product…

We believe this trend will have either a positive or a negative impact on our results of operations, depending on whether we are able to manage our global supply chain effectively, including the accurate forecast of demand, the successful procurement and transportation of raw materials and products, and the effective management of our inventory, production and distribution.

Our ability to generate positive cash flow from operations in the future will be, at least in part, dependent on global economic conditions and our ability to navigate the challenging macro environment at times.

As of September 30, 2026, we were in compliance with the financial covenants under all of our loan agreements, and do not expect material uncertainties in our continued ability to be in compliance with all financial covenants through the remaining term of all of our loan agreements.
In April 2026, we submitted refund claims totaling $25.8 million eligible for processing at time of filing and expect to submit the remaining eligible claims once CBP opens the filing window.
We currently expect to receive the refund of the remaining $1.5 million within the next 12 months, and continue to closely monitor the status of our submitted claims and developments.

Additionally, on November 3, 2026, our Board of Directors declared a regular quarterly cash dividend of $0.47 per share on our common stock, which will be paid on or about November 27, 2026 to shareholders of record at the close of business on November 19, 2026.

We currently believe that our cash on hand, ongoing cash flows from our operations and funding available under our borrowings will be adequate to meet our working capital needs, service our debt, including the entire balance due on our 2027 Term Loan upon maturity, make lease payments, and fund capital expenditures for at least the next 12 months.

In the event we are unable to obtain additional financing when needed, we may be compelled to delay or curtail our plans to develop our business, which could have a material adverse effect on our operations, market position and competitiveness.
Notwithstanding the potential liquidity challenges described above, we expect to meet our long-term liquidity needs with cash flows from operations and financing arrangements.

estimates.t: The following discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations are based upon our condensed consolidated financial statements, which have been prepared in accordance with US GAAP.

statements.t: “With continued success in new account wins and the strength in our pipeline, we remain confident in our long-term growth prospects.

More notably, we successfully built on the relationships we started with these customers and won additional new business with them across multiple product lines in the third quarter, with shipments expected to commence in early 2027.
In addition, we gained four additional chain accounts in the third quarter, with shipments expected to commence in the first half of 2027.

We believe these efforts, combined with the continued strength of our online channel, new chain account wins, and the opening of our new Florida distribution center expected in November 2026, position us well to accelerate revenue growth and improve operating performance in the quarters ahead,” Yu added.

With respect to our financial targets for the 2026 fourth quarter and 2026 full year adjusted EBITDA margin, a reconciliation of these non-GAAP measures to the corresponding GAAP measures is not available without unreasonable effort due to the variability and complexity of the reconciling items described above that we exclude from these non-GAAP target measures.
